text: Chapter 2 starts here: the data structures you'll use constantly for AI work. First up, the most common one — lists.
A list is an ordered, changeable collection. Indexing starts at 0. Negative indices count from the end, so -1 is always the last item. A slice like [0:2] pulls a sub-list.
append adds one item to the end. extend adds multiple items at once. sort sorts in place. len tells you how many items there are, and in checks membership.

A list comprehension builds a new list by transforming or filtering an existing one, in one readable line instead of a multi-line for loop: [expression for item in iterable], with an optional if to filter.
Shaping data is most of what you do integrating with an AI API. A comprehension is exactly how you'd pull just the text out of a batch of API responses.
Lists handle ordered data. Next up: dictionaries — the structure behind every JSON request and response you'll send to an AI API.
